speaker: Laura
text: Welcome to the Q3 business review. Marc, the numbers first.

speaker: Marc
text: Good quarter. Our ARR passed twelve million, up forty percent on last year.

speaker: Laura
text: How much of that came from existing customers?

speaker: Marc
text: A lot. NRR is at one hundred and eighteen percent, so current customers grow their spend every year.

speaker: Marc
text: Gross margin dropped to seventy-one percent because of higher hosting costs.

speaker: Laura
text: And profitability?

speaker: Marc
text: EBITDA is still negative, minus two million, but better than planned.

speaker: Sam
text: On sales, the CAC payback is fourteen months, down from nineteen.

speaker: Laura
text: Explain that for everyone, Sam.

speaker: Sam
text: It's how long a new customer takes to pay back what we spent to win them.

speaker: Marc
text: And with an LTV of about ninety thousand euros per customer, each deal is clearly worth it.

speaker: Sam
text: For Q4 we have three times pipeline coverage, so I'm confident about the target.

speaker: Laura
text: Good. Let's make sure finance and sales use the same numbers.

speaker: Laura
text: {listener}, could you build one shared dashboard for revenue and deals in progress by next Monday?

speaker: Marc
text: Thank you. Now the bigger picture.

speaker: Laura
text: The market is moving fast. Our TAM in Europe alone is about four billion euros.

speaker: Sam
text: So we're barely scratching the surface.

speaker: Laura
text: That's why the board wants to raise a Series B early next year.

speaker: Marc
text: Raising thirty million at our valuation means about eighteen percent dilution for current shareholders.

speaker: Sam
text: What would the money go to?

speaker: Laura
text: Mostly sales in Germany and the Nordics, and a bigger support team.

speaker: Marc
text: Before that, we need to control OpEx: costs grew faster than revenue this quarter.

speaker: Laura
text: Then no new tools or contractors without approval until December.

speaker: Marc
text: Investors will look closely at our unit economics, so every euro has to show a return.

speaker: Sam
text: Our biggest deals are fine; it's the small customers that cost us money to serve.

speaker: Laura
text: Then let's raise the minimum contract size next quarter.

speaker: Marc
text: I'll model the impact on cancellations before we decide.

speaker: Laura
text: {listener}, can you prepare a one-page summary of these numbers for the board meeting on the fifteenth?

speaker: Laura
text: Thanks, everyone. Strong quarter, now let's keep the discipline.
